(This appears to be an excerpt from a larger journal that was written by Zommoros.)

Djinnspit is the most popular vintage of wine in Elona. I take issue with that—not simply because it's a subpar wine manufactured by soulless husks of vintners who care more for money than the art of wine making. Quite simply, it's deceptive marketing.

When it comes to proper Elonian wine, there are numerous alternatives to the run-of-the-mill Djinnspit (hereafter referred to as "common swill").

A few years ago, some foolhardy adventurer tossed down four bottles of Seborhin 1071, a delightful and most unfortunately rare vintage with hints of jammy, but not overpowering, blackberry, anise, vanilla, and just the subtlest touch of licorice. However, that is not my favorite.

No, my favorite is, most surprisingly, something I'd consider a throwaway: Jackspruce Jacaranda. It is not made with jacaranda, of course, but seems to be a grape blend taken from all across the Crystal Oasis. The label is drawn with a most endearing style (showing a jacaranda summoning a lightning bolt into a wine glass), but it is the flavor combination that is most memorable, with a strong and ever-changing floral aroma that evokes the feeling of flying over the Crystal Oasis's most beautiful locales.

My wine collection has grown to a most absurd size, but due to the...UNIQUE conditions that exist within my realm, wine never seems to spoil. Therefore, it would seem I have plenty of time to sample the others to see where they fall in my ever-expanding list of favorites.

Quivering Warmth jammed the tip of her spear into the training dummy, almost yelling out in frustration in the process. It felt good to work out some of her anger. And she had a lot to be angry about, with her ex-boyfriend Devious Weasel trying to get her in trouble with the local Claw.  
  
And then there was that strange newcomer, Rigid Branch... She gripped tighter onto the length of the spear shaft, thinking of those big paws of his. All of these other bearkin sent her into torpor, but that one...  
  
A spear whipped past her, planting itself into the dummy's head and snapping her out of her thoughts. She looked back to see Rigid Branch approaching, holding another spear in his hand already. "Wow," she thought, staring at it. "That's the biggest spear I've ever seen. Is that why they call him Rigid Branch?"  
  
Quivering Warmth remained frozen, overwhelmed by the moment, as Rigid Branch came over and pulled out the embedded spear. "Already in torpor, you are," he teased. She shook her head at him, flustered.  
  
"You'll never get the job done, gripping it like that," he continued, his paws touching hers. He loosened her grip, transferring her paws over to the longer spear. He stood behind her, setting her feet, showing her how to position for maximum effectiveness.  
  
As his big strong paws wrapped around hers, she couldn't help but wonder if there might be a different reason they called him Rigid Branch.

### Author's Note

I have a tale to tell you, dear reader, of the greatest captain to never sail the mighty seas of Cat Storah. In this book, you'll learn about the captain's Kitty Crew, and maybe even how to find them. But tread carefully—they are the most scratch-throat band of landlubbing varmints this side of the Unending Ocean! 

### Chapter 1—Meow

It all started when Leo, gazing fatefully east across the impossible vastness of the sea, said to himself, "Meow."

He was a creature of brevity, it's true. But I think what he meant by this was, "I will assemble a crew of the most scratch-throat band of landlubbing varmints this side of the Unending Ocean! Together, we will sail to our legendary ancestral home of Tear Eeyuh, where the rain is dry, and the milk flows in rivers of frothy white—"

And so on.

To begin filling out his crew, he wisely decided that first he would need a cabin boy to serve his treats and fluff his blankets on the long journey eastward.

"Skippy loves treats and blankets," thought Leo. "As do I. Likely he is basking in the red-leafed shade of Soaring Sands."

"Meow," he said determinedly. And so the journey of Captain Leo the Relentless began.

Frode,  
  
Hate to report back with next to nothing, but most of our research on the isles lived and died in Mabon's head, and Isgarren has most of Mabon's journals set aside for himself. I'll see if I can work on that. Most everything else is code or scraps.  
  
I did manage to pull some information on a village called Gavril. It's fixed—or was—somewhere in the southernmost isle. The single town record we have in the library is dated 1069 AE... You'll never guess whose name is on it, either. Saul D'Alessio. Doesn't that just brighten your day?  
  
We know how that story ended (good riddance to the bastard), but it should make for an interesting excavation. At least this will be a fine opportunity to get hands-on with the area. First time in centuries the region wasn't explicitly under Mabon's watch. Didn't even take me.  
  
I'll send you whatever else I can find. If I do.  
  
—Galrath  
  
PS. Appreciate the desk work. Not eager to make new friends after the last few months I've had. Sitting at a table for a few hours, reading some books, and then taking a long tea break is just what these bitter bones needed.
